source.author: Zephyr-Blessed

commits.subject: Enable ruff UP (pyupgrade) rule and fix all 56 violations

source.description:
## Summary

Enables the ruff `UP` (pyupgrade) rule set and fixes all 56 existing violations across 17 files.

## Changes

| Rule | Description | Count |
|------|-------------|-------|
| UP006 | Use builtin `tuple`/`dict`/`list` instead of `typing.Tuple`/`Dict`/`List` | 29 |
| UP012 | Remove unnecessary `.encode('utf-8')` calls | 10 |
| UP028 | Replace `yield`-over-`for` with `yield from` | 6 |
| UP035 | Import from `collections.abc` instead of `typing` | 5 |
| UP032 | Use f-strings instead of `.format()` | 2 |
| UP031 | Modernize percent string formatting | 2 |
| UP015 | Remove redundant `open()` modes | 2 |

The `UP` rule is now enabled in `pyproject.toml` alongside the existing `E`, `F`, `I`, `B`, `PIE` rules to prevent regressions.

All existing ruff checks continue to pass.

coverage.note: Every hunk read in full. The streaming chain around the six rewritten loops was resolved against the checkout.
limitations: The 56 violation counts in the description are the author's; the diff was read as it stands, not re-linted.

story.headline: One lint rule is switched on. The other sixteen files are what switching it on produced.

beats.label: Was
beats.text: `[tool.ruff.lint] select` listed five rule sets. `UP` was not among them.

beats.label: Now
beats.text: `UP` is listed, and the 56 pre-existing violations are rewritten across 16 files.

beats.label: Watch
beats.text: Six of those rewrites turn a `for`/`yield` loop into `yield from`, which delegates differently.

intent_delta.stated: Enables the ruff `UP` (pyupgrade) rule set and fixes all 56 existing violations across 17 files.

change_map.summary: One line of config, six loops that became delegations, and 50 rewrites with no runtime difference.

groups.summary: The decision. Every other file in this diff follows from it.

groups.summary: The five library rewrites where the two forms are not interchangeable.

files.note: The stream every response goes through, whichever transport produced it.
One `yield from` inside an exception-mapping block, and `SOCKET_OPTION` rewritten.
The iterable here comes from the WSGI application under test, not from httpx.
One `yield from` over a caller-supplied iterator, plus six imports moved to `collections.abc`.
One `yield from` over an internal generator, one f-string, and one `%` that became `.format`.

groups.summary: Aliases that are evaluated at import, not stored as annotation strings.

groups.label: Test files
groups.summary: One rewritten loop, and 18 rewrites with no runtime difference.

files.note: The sixth `yield from`, in the WSGI application the transport tests run against.
`typing.Dict` to `dict` in the ASGI type aliases the test app is annotated with.
`open(..., "r", ...)` loses its mode argument; `r` is what `open` uses anyway.

behavior.summary: Iterating any of these streams yields the same bytes. What differs is what reaches the inner iterator when a consumer closes or throws into the outer generator.

deltas.summary: `close()` and `throw()` on the outer generator now reach the inner iterator.
Every other rewrite yields identical bytes and identical types.

steps.title: The line that caused the other sixteen files
steps.why: One rule set added to `select`. Reading it first turns the rest of the diff into a consequence rather than a list.

annotations.text: `ignore` is unchanged, so no `UP` rule is exempted. Future contributions are held to this too.

steps.title: The six loops that became delegations
steps.why: The only rewrites in the diff where the two forms are not interchangeable, so they are the ones worth reading as code.

annotations.text: `yield from` forwards `close()`, `throw()` and `send()` to the iterator it delegates to. The `for` loop did not.
This one delegates inside `with map_httpcore_exceptions():`, so the block is what an exception from the inner iterator still passes through.
The iterable here is whatever the WSGI application returned, and PEP 3333 gives it an optional `close`.
`self._stream` here is the iterator a caller passed as request content.

steps.title: Type aliases, which are evaluated and not annotations
steps.why: These lines run at import rather than being stored as strings, so the builtin generics must be subscriptable. `requires-python` is `>=3.9`.

annotations.text: Six names move from `typing` to `collections.abc`. Both are re-exported by this module's `Union` aliases below.
`CookieTypes` and its neighbours are what a caller passes to `httpx.Client`, so these are the annotations users see.

steps.title: The two string rewrites
steps.why: The only places where the produced string is built differently rather than typed differently.

annotations.text: `%s` became `.format(...)` rather than an f-string, so the wrapped call stays where it was.

checks.title: Closing a response now reaches the transport's iterator
checks.why: `yield from` forwards `close()` inward, so a consumer abandoning a streamed response can now close an httpcore stream or a WSGI application's output.
checks.question: Do any of your custom transports return an iterable whose `close()` does more than release a connection?

checks.title: `_types.py` is where user-facing annotations are declared
checks.why: `QueryParamTypes`, `HeaderTypes` and `CookieTypes` are evaluated at import and used in the signatures callers type against. A tool reading them sees `list[...]`.
checks.question: Does anything you run inspect these aliases at runtime, such as a docs builder or a settings library?

checks.title: The rule applies to every future pull request
checks.why: `UP` stays in `select` after this merges, so ruff will reject the older spellings in contributions from now on, not only in these 17 files.
checks.question: Is holding contributors to pyupgrade's rewrites the standard you want for incoming pull requests?

skippable.label: Encoding and mode rewrites in tests
skippable.reason: Eight test files where `.encode("utf-8")` loses its argument, `open(..., "r")` loses its mode, and `typing.Dict` becomes `dict`.
